intro: The Ramayana is one of the best-loved stories in the world. It tells of Prince Rama, his wife Sita, his brother Lakshmana and their loyal helper Hanuman. Hindu tradition honors the sage Valmiki as its first poet.

In this unit you will follow the whole story, from the palace in Ayodhya to the forest, to Lanka and home again. You will see how the poem teaches dharma, doing what is right for your role. You will also see how readers ask hard questions and tell the story in many new ways.
By the end, you will be able to retell the main events in order. You will be able to explain dharma with examples. You will be able to compare two tellings of the Ramayana fairly.
bigQuestion: What does the Ramayana teach about doing what is right, and why do people tell it in so many ways?

timeline.t: Scholars date Valmiki's Ramayana to between about 500 BCE and 100 CE
Bala Kanda: Rama's birth and childhood; he marries Sita
Ayodhya Kanda: Kaikeyi's boons; Rama goes into exile
Aranya Kanda: life in the forest; Ravana carries Sita away
Kishkindha Kanda: Rama allies with Sugriva and Hanuman
Sundara Kanda: Hanuman finds Sita in Lanka
Yuddha Kanda: the battle; Rama returns and is crowned
Uttara Kanda: later events, including Sita's exile
Chandrabati writes a Bengali Ramayana; Tulsidas writes the Ramcharitmanas

one of the seven books of the Ramayana

being sent away from your home
duty, or the right way to live for your role in life
Ravana's island kingdom in the Ramayana
one of the monkey people who help Rama
"the rule of Rama"; an ideal of fair and peaceful government
the poet who retold the Ramayana in a form of Hindi in the 1500s
a play of Rama's life, often performed over many nights
the point of view from which a story is told

test.q: Whom does tradition honor as the Ramayana's first poet?
test.why: Tradition calls Valmiki the first poet.

test.q: How many kandas are in Valmiki's Ramayana?
Why does Rama go into exile?
choices: To keep his father's promise to Kaikeyi
test.why: Rama goes so that Dasharatha's word to Kaikeyi is kept.

test.q: What does Bharata do with Rama's sandals?
test.why: Bharata rules in Rama's name with the sandals on the throne.

test.q: In the Ramayana, what does dharma mean?
choices: Doing what is right for your role
test.why: Dharma is right action for one's role.

test.q: Which kanda follows Hanuman to Lanka?
What does Sita do when Ravana asks her to marry him?
test.why: Sita refuses Ravana and stays loyal to Rama.

test.q: Who leads the building of the bridge in Valmiki's poem?
test.why: The vanara Nala leads the building.

test.q: Whom does Rama make king of Lanka?
test.why: Rama makes Vibhishana king of Lanka.
Rama Rajya means the rule of Rama, an ideal of fair government.

test.q: How do readers respond to Sita's treatment in the Uttara Kanda?
choices: In different ways, and many retellings take Sita's side
They say Sita was not in the story
test.why: Readers respond in many ways, and many tellings center Sita.
Tulsidas wrote it in a form of Hindi.

choices: A woman poet of a Bengali Ramayana
test.why: Chandrabati wrote a Bengali Ramayana in the 1500s.

test.q: Which festival often ends the Ramlila?
test.why: Many Ramlilas end at Dussehra, the festival of Rama's victory.

write.prompt: Which character in the Ramayana best shows dharma? Choose one: Rama, Bharata, Lakshmana or Sita. Use two scenes from the unit, naming the kanda (for example, Ayodhya Kanda or Sundara Kanda). Explain what the poem says and how Hindus have read it.
tips: Name the kanda for each scene you use.
Write "the poem says" or "many Hindus see" when you tell a belief.
Explain what the character's role is and how they live up to it.
Use at least three words from this unit.
